articles.title: TikTok reaches first state settlement in US over teen safety claims, agrees to user limits
articles.summary: Alabama secures $100 million settlement with TikTok, mandating new usage limits and age-verification measures to protect teens, as the state claims the platform endangers youth and misleads consumers…

blocks.text: Alabama said on Friday it had reached a settlement with TikTok and its Chinese parent company, ByteDance, that requires the social media platform to impose new usage limits and enhanced age-verification measures for users in the state, resolving claims that the platform endangered children and misled consumers about its safety.

The agreement, which came days before a scheduled trial, calls for TikTok to implement changes for teenagers in Alabama including a two-hour daily time limit, pauses after 15 minutes of use and stricter age checks.

TikTok will pay Alabama at least $100 million under the settlement, but the state’s payout could grow to $300 million if 40 other attorneys general sign on to similar agreements with the company within a specified timeframe, according to the settlement.
“This builds on our commitment and core objective to continually enhance our robust safety tools to protect teens,” a spokesperson for TikTok’s US operations said in a statement.

The deal marks TikTok’s first settlement with a state in the sweeping litigation over social media’s impact on teen well-being. Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall sued the company last year, and at least 27 other states and Washington, D.C., have brought similar lawsuits.
“This is a great day for Alabama parents,” Marshall said in announcing the agreement.

The trial, which had been scheduled to kick off Monday in Montgomery state court and expected to last two to three weeks, had been expected to provide a rare look inside TikTok, which has settled prior cases selected for trial and sought to keep details of its operations from public view.

Alabama had claimed TikTok’s endless stream of videos makes it the most addictive social media platform and that its algorithm pushes young users toward increasingly intense content about violence and self-harm, contributing to a teen mental health crisis and causing the number of emergency room visits for self-harm in the state to “skyrocket.”

The lawsuit accused TikTok of falsely claiming it limits access to sexual and violent content for young users in order to have its app rated safe for teens in app stores run by Google, Apple and Microsoft and of misleading users about the Chinese government’s access to US users’ data.

TikTok has said it designed its platform with teen safety as a key priority and argued that Section 230 of the federal Communications Decency Act shields online platforms from liability over user-generated content.

In addition to the states’ cases, TikTok faces thousands of lawsuits by individuals, school districts and municipalities over its alleged impact on young users’ mental health. Meta Platforms, Snap Inc and Alphabet’s YouTube are also defendants in many of these cases.
With the settlement in Alabama, TikTok has settled all cases selected for trial against it, including claims by five young people and a Kentucky school district.

Alabama’s lawsuit claimed TikTok asks users to self-report their ages, but it also allows users to evade its questions about their age by viewing videos without creating an account, which still allows the company to collect data on their viewing habits. The lack of an effective age restriction makes things like “Kids Mode,” which curates content for young users, entirely useless, according to the lawsuit.

The state also claimed the platform traps kids in so-called “filter bubbles,” feeding them increasingly intense content on subjects that capture their attention, including violent or harmful material.

Last month, ​Meta reached a sweeping $17.1 billion settlement with 47 states, Washington, D.C., and US territories. Meta, which ​did not admit wrongdoing, agreed to make changes to teens’ access to Instagram and Facebook as part of the deal and conditioned $5 billion of the payout on TikTok, Snap ​and YouTube’s adoption of those terms. TikTok has not said anything publicly about the deal.
Like the Meta settlement, Alabama’s deal with TikTok would require the company to adopt additional restrictions if its rivals Snap, Google and Meta make similar changes.
Those measures could further limit teens’ time on social media apps and restrict overnight access, according to the filing.
Although the settlement applies only in Alabama, major platform changes could prove difficult to implement on a state-by-state basis. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: India and Pakistan traded accusations at the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on Friday, with Islamabad criticizing India's stance on Kashmir and New Delhi accusing Pakistan of supporting cross-border terrorism.
Addressing the General Assembly, Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif called for "a just and fair resolution of the Kashmir dispute," alleging human rights violations in the region.
Sharif also brought up the military clashes last year between the uneasy neighbors, calling them "external aggression from India under a false pretext."

Pakistan considers Indian missile strikes on May 7 to be the start of the low-level conflict, which ran for less than a week, while India contends that the strikes were retaliation for an attack in Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir in April last year.
He added that India's decision to hold the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance had no legal basis and accused New Delhi of "weaponizing" water.

India rejected Sharif's remarks. First Secretary at India's UN mission Petal Gahlot accused Pakistan of "terrorism, deceit and duplicity" and said Islamabad's support for cross-border terrorism would have consequences.
Gahlot also criticized Pakistan's military establishment and its treatment of minorities, while reiterating India's position that Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of the country.

articles.title: Duterte camp flags 62,000-plus evidence ahead of ICC trial, seeks 10,000 cap
articles.summary: The defense team of former President Rodrigo Duterte has asked the International Criminal Court to limit the prosecution’s evidence to 10,000 items, saying the case record has ballooned to more…

blocks.text: September 26, 2026 | 3:25pm

MANILA, Philippines — The defense team of former President Rodrigo Duterte has asked the International Criminal Court (ICC) to limit the prosecution’s evidence to 10,000 items, saying the case record has ballooned to more than 62,000 items ahead of his trial.
Defense counsel Peter Haynes filed the motion before ICC Trial Chamber III on Friday, September 25, citing the volume and quality of the evidence disclosed by the prosecution.
The defense said the prosecution initially disclosed 5,275 evidence items during the confirmation phase but later expanded the list to 62,130, a 978% increase.
The prosecution’s current List of Evidence contains 19,238 items, according to the defense.

“The Defence has no ability to read this volume of evidence prior to trial. However, even a cursory review demonstrates that much of the disclosed material is of extremely limited or no relevance to the charges in this case,” Haynes said.
The defense said the disclosure includes more than 320,000 pages of documents and 1,000 audio-visual materials.

“The sheer volume of material, disclosed to the Defence three months before the start of trial, undermines Mr Duterte’s right to adequate time for the preparation of his defence pursuant to Article 67(1)(b),” Haynes said.
The defense estimated that reviewing all the documentary evidence just once would take about 16,000 person-hours.
“On a conservative estimate of three minutes per page, it would take 16,000 person hours to review every disclosed item of documentary evidence just once,” Haynes said.

The defense also flagged problems with the evidence, including incorrect descriptions, dates and metadata, detached pages, illegible or blank items, duplicate documents, and untranslated or untranscribed audio and video files.
They said proceeding with the case under the current disclosure would also affect Duterte’s right to a timely trial.
“Proceeding to trial on this basis would undermine the efficiency of proceedings and, by consequence, Mr Duterte’s right to trial without undue delay,” Haynes said.
Defense asks for 10,000-item case record
Instead of seeking to postpone the trial, the defense proposed that the prosecution sort through the evidence and create a new case record containing a maximum of 10,000 items.
The proposed record would include exculpatory evidence, as well as duly reviewed and triaged Rule 77 and incriminating evidence.
“A reduction from 62,130 to 10,000 is significant,” the defense said.
They said the remaining evidence would still be accessible to Duterte’s lawyers, who would have to “read, watch, listen to, review and tag” the original case record.
Haynes asked the chamber to order the prosecution to work with the ICC Registry to create the new case record by October 7.
The defense said this would allow the trial to proceed as scheduled on November 30.
Duterte’s defense team is due to file its pre-trial brief on October 30.
Duterte remains detained
Duterte remains detained at the ICC in The Hague, where he faces crimes against humanity charges over killings linked to his war on drugs.
The 81-year-old former president appeared in person before the ICC on September 16 during the third status conference.

articles.title: Bangkok roads submerged as flood disaster declared
articles.summary: An emergency has been declared across the capital of Thailand as days of heavy rain leave the city inundated.

blocks.text: Disaster declared as heavy rain sparks Bangkok flooding
A flood emergency disaster has been declared across Bangkok after 48 hours of heavy rain left roads in the Thai capital submerged.
People have been urged to stay at home and those living close to the city's network of canals have been advised to move their belongings to upper floors.

Thunderstorms are common in Thailand at this time of year but extreme weather in recent days has inundated Bangkok's drainage system, causing traffic chaos on roads that are already famously congested.
The rain is expected to continue into Sunday, raising fears that more canals could burst their banks.
Image source, Getty Images
Canals across the Thai capital have burst their banks, leaving roads under water
Somkid Pheuk-ngam, a 67-year-old who lives near a canal just north of central Bangkok, told the AFP news agency: "The water keeps coming in. It's hard to go out now. It's like at my waist level now.
"I cannot go anywhere. I have been closing my shop for two days now."
She said water levels in the city appeared to be worse than in 2011, when Bangkok was impacted by nationwide flooding.
Hundreds were killed across Thailand then in an extreme weather event that lasted for three months. So far, no casualties have been reported in Bangkok from this latest flooding.
The Thai Meteorological Service has forecast more heavy rain through the week, though the area of low pressure causing the downpours of recent days is expected to move towards central Thailand.

blocks.caption: People holding umbrellas and walking down a narrow flooded street in Bangkok

blocks.text: All 50 of Bangkok's districts have been declared emergency zones.
Chadchart Sittipunt, the city's governor, said the east of the city had been hardest hit, AFP reported.

He continued: "The rain keeps falling and we are doing our best. We are trying to pump the water out, but the water in canals are full... The risk areas are those who live near canals. Every canal is now filled."

MANILA, Philippines – UE will once again open a new chapter in its men’s basketball program.
Chris Gavina is no longer the coach of the Red Warriors as interim head coach Paolo Hubalde takes over the reins during their match against the FEU Tamaraws on Saturday, September 26.
Hubalde, a former PBA player and UE legend who returned to the Red Warriors’ program as an assistant coach in Season 89, is expected to be the team’s head coach for the rest of the season.
The coaching change comes as UE battles through a 22-game losing streak dating back to Season 87 in October 2024.
Gavina was not on the bench for UE’s game on Saturday. Assistant coaches Alex Cabagnot and Nick Demusis were also absent.
The Red Warriors opened the current season with losses to the Ateneo Blue Eagles by 27 points, and the NU Bulldogs by 20 points, extending a difficult stretch for the program.
Gavina leaves UE without a win in 16 games after taking over from Jack Santiago in 2025.
Santiago led the Red Warriors to six victories before UE fell in a playoff for the No. 4 seed in Season 87, missing a chance to make its first Final Four appearance in 15 years.
Hubalde now inherits a young roster featuring Nur Datumalim, Cole Cruz-Dumont, Tope Lagat and foreign reinforcements JM Edoukou and Ola Ajani.
The former UE point guard played for the Red Warriors in the mid-2000s, when the program featured stars such as Paul Artadi, James Yap, Niño Canaleta and Ronald Tubid.
Hubalde returns to a very different UE team, one still searching for stability and its first win of the season.
Hubalde will also balance his new role with his duties as UE’s junior high school basketball coach.
He will have help from active consultant Allan Caidic, another name linked to the head coaching vacancy, along with assistant coach RJ Argamino.
For UE, the change marks another attempt to turn the page and begin rebuilding the Red Warriors into a competitive program. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Rare sale of David Hockney painting of beloved dog Stanley could fetch £2.5m
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Dog Painting 17 is believed to be one of only six of works from Dog Series in private hands and first to be auctioned

David Hockney adored his dachshunds Stanley and Boodgie and…
articles.byline: Mark Brown North of England correspondent

blocks.text: David Hockney adored his dachshunds Stanley and Boodgie and let them run riot – so much so that after one had an accident in the LA home of the actor Dennis Hopper, the painter is said to have quipped: “It’ll be dry in the morning, luv, and you can just pick it up.”
But Hockney did not just indulge his four-legged companions, he treated them as portrait subjects for a series of paintings, one of which is to be sold by Christie’s.

The piece is the first from a series of dog paintings by Hockney, who died in June, ever to appear at auction. “This is such an exciting painting for us,” said Tessa Lord, Christie’s head of postwar and contemporary art. “The rarity is kind of extraordinary.”

The painting is titled Dog Painting 17 and shows Hockney’s first dachshund, Stanley, curled up on a cushion, fast asleep. It has an estimate of £1.5m-£2.5m and is one of more than 40 works that Hockney painted in 1994-95 for his Dog Series.
Stanley, named after Stan Laurel, was picked out as a puppy by Hockney in 1987 and followed him around constantly. Boodgie, more reserved, arrived later.

blocks.caption: Hockney holding one of his dachshunds in 1993. Photograph: Photo Researchers/Getty Images

blocks.text: According to Hockney’s authorised biographer Christopher Simon Sykes, friends of the peripatetic Hockney were astonished he was getting a dog in the first place. But they soon saw how besotted he was.
The feeling was mutual and the noisy dachshunds soon became an essential part of his busy friend- and visitor-filled life in his Hollywood Hills home on Montcalm Avenue.
Sykes in his biography writes that Hockney was not bothered about house training, with one friend, Jonathon Brown, recalling how the dogs used to defecate in his shoes.
On a visit by Hockney for dinner at Hopper’s Frank Gehry-designed house in Venice, LA, Boodgie left a “gift” in the middle of the floor.

According to Brown, Hockney did retrospectively wag his finger, telling Boodgie “no, NO!”. Then, “as Hopper’s look of a chain-gang murderer increased in intensity, Hockney added: “Oah, it’ll be dry in the morning, luv, and you can just pick it up.”
Hopper, the story goes, was left with two choices: silence or murder. “He chose silence, but he looked like murder.”
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Hockney at his Los Angeles home in 1987. Photograph: Anthony Barboza/Getty Images

blocks.text: Hockney embarked on his dog paintings when he needed some sunshine in his life. He had lost several friends to Aids and was devastated by the death of one of his closest, oldest friends, Henry Geldzahler, to pancreatic cancer. The artist told one journalist he wanted “desperately to paint something loving”.
Lord said: “He felt such a loss of love, this was kind of a catharsis for him.”
Christie’s believes there are only six of the dog paintings in private hands, with the others owned by the David Hockney Foundation.

The seller of Dog Painting 17 bought it after the dog series went on display at the LA Louver gallery, a wildly popular show that Hockney said attracted 7,000 people in four days – many with their own dogs in tow.

Lord said the painting displayed “incredible spontaneity” and “fluidity of brushstrokes, but it still feels richly textured. You’ve got this sort of mottling underneath the cushion and you’ve got that slight flick of the ear that really animates Stanley.”

She said the painting shone light on an important chapter in the life of one of the greatest artists of the 20th and 21st century. “I love the fact that there is this kind of innocence to it but it is so much more than that. There’s a universality to it … it’s so much more than just a portrait of a dog.”
The painting will be sold on 14 October during Frieze Week, and it will go on display – anyone can see it for free – at Christie’s in London from 8 October.

articles.title: ‘I felt shame’: former BA worker locked in legal battle after losing job of 30 years
articles.summary:
Cabin crew worker was among thousands of staff laid off during pandemic in what MPs called a ‘national disgrace’

During a 30-year career as a member of British Airways’ cabin crew, Tess De…

blocks.text: During a 30-year career as a member of British Airways’ cabin crew, Tess De Mello took pride in a job well done, saying she regularly went above and beyond to make passengers more comfortable. To her, the role was more than just employment – it was part of her identity.
“I took pride,” she said. “I really took pride in myself, I took pride in my role, I took pride in everything because it was everything I wanted to be.”

But in 2020 she was let go when BA cut thousands of jobs in the face of economic pressures during the pandemic. The airline issued almost all of its 42,000 staff with redundancy notices, with 10,000 ultimately losing their jobs.

At the time, the Unite union representing cabin crew told the parliamentary transport select committee BA had taken a fire-and-rehire approach, with staff who remained having to accept pay cuts and demotions. MPs called it a “national disgrace”.
De Mello has spent the years since locked in legal battles with BA. It has not only been a courtroom drama but a personal ordeal.

There was a great amount of shame attached to her dismissal, she has said, leaving her fearing what those colleagues who had looked up to her would think upon learning she had been among those not kept on by BA.
“To have that taken away from you … I’ve been thinking, what would that person think about me now? Would they think I’ve done something wrong?
“The shame of being dismissed, for me, it was personal … You think people are going to judge you for doing something wrong.”
She said she was concerned her former colleagues would assume she had not been selected to stay because her performance had been deemed poor.
“I took such pride in my work, in my ability. I was always on top of things,” she said. “The shame stems from losing my job.”
BA had told its longest-serving cabin crew they should expect to take a 20% basic pay cut to be retained. Unite later said salaries dropped by between 15% and 35%.

When De Mello asked for clarification of her exact salary upon being rehired and some time to consider, making sure to say explicitly she wanted to stay with the airline, she was told she would now be treated as if she had decided to leave, according to court documents for an unfair dismissal claim she later made against BA.
Judge Laurie Anstis found against her and a former colleague at an employment tribunal in Reading last year. They are appealing the ruling.
after newsletter promotion
They are also claiming they were underpaid their holiday entitlement while they were part-time workers for BA. If successful, the case could have ramifications across the aviation sector.

Because of the nature of the job, for those on part-time contracts working shorter days is not realistic. This meant working a block of full days on, followed by a block of days off. Their lawyers argue this classified them as “part-year” workers, similar to teachers, who are entitled to full-time holiday.

They cite a 2022 supreme court ruling that said: “The amount of leave to which a part-year worker under a permanent contract is entitled is not required by EU law to be, and under domestic law is not, prorated to that of a full-time worker.”

According to Unite, this type of shift pattern is standard across the industry, meaning that, were De Mello and her former colleague to win, the door would be open to similar claims from many other cabin crew workers – with the potential for huge financial outlay for airlines.

BA said: “In 2025, an employment tribunal dismissed claims brought by the two claimants relating to the steps British Airways took to avoid the collapse of the business and loss of thousands of jobs during the Covid-19 pandemic.

“Finding in our favour and dismissing the claims, that employment tribunal determined that BA’s actions had been non-discriminatory and fair. We believe these latest claims are without merit. We will be making that clear to the tribunal.”

articles.title: Velasco camp: Reports of illegal activities have 'no basis'
articles.summary: The camp of Lord Allan Velasco on Saturday issued a statement on what they called "fabricated attacks' on the former House Speaker, saying the allegations against him have "no basis."

blocks.text: Published September 26, 2026 2:35pm
The camp of Lord Allan Velasco on Saturday issued a statement on what they called "fabricated attacks" on the former House Speaker, saying the allegations against him have "no basis."

"The former Speaker of the House's record of service in the government is untainted with corruption and his wife's benevolence is widely known, leaving no basis for the illegal allegations now being suggested," said Velascos' spokesperson, Atty. Rowell Ilagan in a statement.
Velasco's camp also called the accusations against the former speaker as "inconsistent."

"The "one-size-fits-all" narration by this individual seems to be designed and fabricated to attack as many targets as it can while being inconsistent with verifiable events, that is, the Covid-19 pandemic, Atty.Velasco's period of service as speaker, other details, and even basic common sense," added Velascos' spokesperson.

On Friday, dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr., who claim to have served as a security officer for Velasco, said that he delivered suitcases containing cash to Vice President Sara Duterte, former President Rodrigo Duterte, and Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo Duterte as ordered by the former speaker.
Velasco's camp, however, urges the public to be "more circumspect" about the allegations.

"We respectfully urge everyone to be more circumspect in appreciating this news report while we evaluate and determine the accountability of the individual and the publisher under the law," said Atty. Ilagan.
Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday also denied Gracioso's claim.
"Mga kababayan, I do not know Rodulfo Gracioso Jr., nor have I ever received any money from him," Duterte said in a statement.
"My lawyers are awaiting an official copy of the Gracioso affidavit from the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) so they can begin working on the cases to be filed against him," she added.
"Once we are done dismantling the lies contained in his testimony, it will end up in the trash bin—just like the one from Ramil Madriaga," Duterte said.
The vice president said Gracioso's allegation is "another media stunt," adding that the Marcos administration is bent on bringing her down.

"This is nothing more than another media stunt, an attempt to breathe life into a faltering impeachment case. The desperation of the administration to bring me down, push for Charter Change, prevent the 2028 elections, and cling to power is becoming increasingly diabolical," she said.
Gracioso estimated that he had delivered a total of more than P2 billion to Sara Duterte.
He also said he also brought money to then-President Rodrigo Duterte at Malacañang between 2018 and 2022, and delivered a suitcase containing P100 million to Pulong Duterte.
Justice Secretary Fredderick Vida confirmed in a message to GMA News that the Department of Justice had received Gracioso’s affidavit and was evaluating it.
GMA News has sought comments through phone calls and messages from Pulong Duterte and Rodrigo Duterte since Thursday, but they have yet to give any.
The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) said it is investigating Gracioso's claims. —VAL, GMA News

articles.title: DMW chief Cacdac orders 'comprehensive reintegration' support for Mary Jane Veloso
articles.summary: Migrant Workers Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac has ordered the provision of full reintegration assistance for former overseas Filipino worker (OFW) Mary Jane Veloso following her grant of absolute pardon…

blocks.text: Published September 26, 2026 2:35pm

Migrant Workers Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac has ordered the provision of full reintegration assistance for former overseas Filipino worker (OFW) Mary Jane Veloso following her grant of absolute pardon and subsequent freedom from jail.
In a statement, the DMW said Cacdac has ordered a support team to coordinate with Veloso's family in Nueva Ecija to facilitate her "comprehensive reintegration."
The team is tasked to "lay the groundwork for immediate family- and community-level interventions" that would allow Veloso's long-term productivity and self-sufficiency.
"Our instructions are clear: the DMW must stand shoulder-to-shoulder with Mary Jane, her children, and her parents as they rebuild their lives," Cacdac said.
Cacdac said her "tailored reintegration program" involves direct discussions her family and local stakeholders.
The DMW issued the statement hours after President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. said Friday that he has already signed the order for Veloso's absolute pardon.

On the same day of the President's announcement, Veloso was released from the Correctional Institution for Women (CIW) in Mandaluyong City, turning the page on the 16-year chapter of her life spent behind bars on drug charges.
The DMW said it is working with the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA) to ensure that Veloso's transition to her new life is sustainable.
This involves linking her "ventures directly to local cooperatives and municipal economic opportunities in Nueva Ecija," with the goal that this would foster community participation.
Veloso languished on death row in Indonesia following her arrest in April 2010 at the Adisutjipto International Airport in Yogjakarta for alleged possession of heroin.
Veloso and her supporters have long insisted that she was exploited as drug mule and was actually the victim in the case.
She was sentenced her to death in October 2010, but a strong appeal from the late President Benigno Simeon "Noynoy" Aquino III paved the way for the commutation of her punishment in 2015.
In December 2024, Indonesian authorities agreed to transfer custody over Veloso to the Philippines. — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Thailand: Bangkok flooding triggers disaster declaration
articles.summary: Rainfall over the past three days has caused heavy flooding in the Thai capital. A state of disaster has been declared in all 50 districts in Bangkok.

image.caption: Bangkok's governor said the eastern parts of the city were most impactedImage: Josh Smith/REUTERS

blocks.text: Authorities in Bangkok on Saturday declared a disaster across 50 districts in Thailand's capital after days of heavy rainfall caused severe flooding.
Bangkok Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said the eastern parts of the city were impacted most.

blocks.caption: Bangkok's governor urges residents to move cars to higher groundImage: AP Video/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Situation in brief

items: Governor Chadchart Sittipunt said the situation posed a threat to life
Emergency ​advisory for ⁠people living near canals to move possessions to ​higher ground
Bangkok city officials open shelter for evacuees
More rain forecast into Sunday

blocks.text: More rain in Bangkok forecast
Chadchart said almost 300 millimeters (11.8 inches) of rain had fallen since Thursday afternoon and warned that more rain was expected.

"The rain keeps falling and we are doing our best. We are trying to pump the water out, but the water in canals are full," the governor said on social media and advised residents to move their possessions to higher ground.
"The risk areas are those who live near canals. Every canal is now filled," he said.
Chadchart urged bedridden patients dependent on life-saving medical equipment to consider a temporary stay in hospital.

blocks.caption: Thailand's Meteorological Department warned the heavy rain would persist in most parts of the country through SundayImage: Alex Ogle/AFP

blocks.text: Floods evoke memories of deadly 2011 deluge
"The water keeps coming in. It's hard to go out now. It's like at my waist level now," local vendor Somkid Pheuk-ngam, told the AFP news agency.
"I cannot go anywhere. I have been closing my shop for two days now," she told AFP, adding that while she often gets flooded, "I think this time is worse than the 2011 flood."
Flooding across Thailand in 2011 killed more than 500 people and damaged millions of homes.

Thailand's Meteorological Department warned the heavy rain would persist in most parts of the country through Sunday and pointed to a strong low-pressure system dominating the central region and strengthening monsoon conditions.

articles.title: ‘The weaker he gets, the more dangerous he gets’: Trump lashes out as his power wanes
articles.summary:
Trump tries to dominate at the UN as his approval ratings plummet and even some Republicans stray from the script

Donald Trump…

blocks.text: Donald Trump stood before the United Nations on Tuesday and threatened to “annihilate” Iran. Yet even as the most powerful man on the planet flexed his military muscles, he was powerless to keep the gravitational pull of domestic politics at bay.

Heading into the UN building in New York, the US president was questioned by Kaitlan Collins, an anchor at CNN, which he had banned from the White House before a judge ruled against him. “I’m surprised that CNN is here covering me,” the 80-year-old snapped. “You should not be here covering me.”

The lashing-out was a reminder that even Trump, who has expanded executive power and dominated the national consciousness, finds some things beyond his control. Indeed, 20 months into his second term, there is a widening gap between the president’s self-perceived invincibility and the reality of his waning influence.

Federal courts are reining him in. Congressional Republicans are straying from the script. Poll numbers are tumbling to historic depths, driven by persistent inflation, rising fuel costs and an increasingly unpopular war in Iran. For the first time since his improbable political resurrection, Trump’s aura of authority is fading.

Rick Wilson, a longtime Republican strategist, prophesied: “This is the beginning of the end. This is the decline. As powerful and transgressive as he’s been, the country does not have a positive outlook right now. In fact, the negativity and pessimism among voters has reached a point that is unparalleled since Jimmy Carter.”

Trump’s self-belief never wavers. He faced four criminal cases and two assassination attempts before winning the 2024 election. He has lived by a mantra of “it will all work out well in the end” while his supporters wear hats that state: “Trump was right about everything.”

Yet he has had a rough month. The Federal Reserve defied him on interest rates. The supreme court blocked his administration’s attempt to impose new restrictions on mail-in ballots for November’s midterm elections. One judge prevented him adding his name to the Kennedy Center, prompting him to threaten the national arts complex with demolition; another judge blocked his ban on three news outlets from the White House grounds, ordering the administration to “immediately return, reinstate and restore” their access.

Now even Trump’s dependable power base, the Republican party, is showing cracks amid fears that he will cost them seats in November. In Florida, his home state, gubernatorial candidate Byron Donalds quietly scrubbed most Trump references from his campaign website, while the congresswoman María Elvira Salazar ran campaign advertisements openly declaring that federal immigration enforcement had gone “too far” and asserting that Latino voters “feel betrayed”.

blocks.caption: Byron Donalds, the Republican candidate for Florida governor, has distanced himself from Trump. Photograph: Joe Raedle/Getty Images

blocks.text: Wilson, a co-founder of the Lincoln Project, an anti-Trump group, sees a herd mentality among congressional Republicans and compares the current mood to a wildlife documentary.

“It needs a David Attenborough voiceover,” he said. “It’s like the gazelles wandering the savannah. They’re sniffing the wind now and they smell something in the wind. They know it’s a predator but they don’t know what to do about it yet. What they haven’t realised is that the predator has been among them all along. The risk factor that they face now is Trump.”

For nearly a decade, elected Republicans maintained a posture of submission, fearful of drawing a primary challenger or a scathing post on Truth Social. But with the elections looming and control of Congress hanging in the balance, self-preservation is rapidly overriding loyalty to the president.

Wilson said: “Now it’s reached the point where the magic doesn’t work any more. There’s no political upside from a president who is at 29% approval rating in some polls, has presided over a disastrous war, and has ended up raising energy prices and food prices – all the things that they can’t spin away.
“The voters now have very much put that together. They associate the war with Trump. They associate the gas prices with Trump. They associate the grocery prices with Trump.”

blocks.caption: Gas prices on 22 September 2026 in Doral, Florida. Photograph: Lynne Sladky/AP

blocks.text: This creates a vicious circle, Wilson argues. “The more he becomes a liability, the more he acts out. The more he demands loyalty from people and doesn’t get it, the more he demands loyalty from people and doesn’t get it. Everything was handed to him for a decade by that party and, now that they’re paying the price, they’ve decided this has got a little too hairy.”

Faced with shrinking authority and a hostile economic landscape, Trump has reverted to his trusted playbook: manufacturing spectacle, picking cultural fights and raging against the press. His recent decision to ban the news outlets CNN, MS Now and Politico from the White House campus following critical coverage was viewed by critics not as a display of strength, but a symptom of deep frustration.

The administration rejects such charges and insists that the president’s agenda is succeeding. Davis Ingle, a White House spokesperson, said in an email: “President Trump is the unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party, and he is committed to maintaining Republican majorities in Congress.

“The president signed the largest working-class tax cuts in history, lowered the cost of prescription drugs, sealed the border, drove violent crime to the lowest level in nearly a century, unleashed an energy revolution, added more than a million private-sector jobs, and sent Americans’ 401(k)s climbing to record highs,” he added. “The choice has never been more clear: doubling down on President Trump’s winning, commonsense agenda or the Democrats’ extreme liberal policies and obstruction.”

But the trend lines are only set to worsen for Trump. If Democrats gain control of the House of Representatives next year, they plan to launch investigations into how he has allegedly abused his office to enrich his family, grant favours to supporters, hollow out the federal government and carry out expensive construction projects. The attention economy, meanwhile, will inexorably shift to the 2028 presidential race and the question of succession.

Bill Galston, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution thinktank in Washington, said the inevitable shift of focus toward potential candidates – such as the vice-president, JD Vance, or the secretary of state, Marco Rubio – will be cause for friction.

“Nothing will drive him crazier than the shift of the spotlight away from him,” said Galston, a former domestic policy adviser to Bill Clinton. “The prospect of passing the torch, giving up the spotlight, is intensely painful for him. It’s his oxygen. Will he be able to breathe, spiritually and emotionally speaking, without it?”

Trump is not the first president to run into trouble after winning re-election. From Richard Nixon’s Watergate downfall to Clinton’s impeachment and George W Bush’s quagmire in Iraq, second terms have historically served as the graveyard of presidential ambition.

Allan Lichtman, author of a new book, Great American Presidents: The Twelve Who Transformed the Nation, calls it “the second term curse”. He noted: “Second terms have been remarkably difficult for presidents.”

blocks.caption: Donald Trump arrives at the 81st United Nations general assembly in New York on 22 September 2026. Photograph: Timothy A Clary/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: Lichtman, a history professor at American University in Washington, believes that Trump is driven by two things: money and glory. “He cannot stand not being the centre of attention and that’s dangerous,” he said. “I don’t care much about his verbal lashing-out; I don’t think that helps him at all. But who knows what crazy things he might do to reassert attention on him? And that’s frightening.

“Never underestimate the power of the president. Just because Republicans are criticising him, his poll numbers are low, prospects for Republicans look dim, doesn’t mean he doesn’t have enormous power – and he is certainly quite willing to use that power unconstrained. He doesn’t care about the courts and doesn’t care about the Congress.”

From this perspective, Trump’s last refuge will be the unchecked use of executive authority, a politicised justice department and a sweeping pardon power. With nothing to lose in his final two years, he could go out all guns blazing.

Charlie Sykes, a conservative author and broadcaster, said: “Donald Trump fears irrelevance more than anything and he’ll rage against it as long as he can. The notion that he will go quietly would be incredibly naive.

“We’re headed for a collision between a lame duck who has no respect for the constitutional norms and an opposition that may have some power to hold him accountable. The paradox is the weaker he gets, the more dangerous he gets.”

articles.title: From Baguio to Sepang, Iñigo Anton gears up for biggest race of his career in F1 weekend
articles.summary: With a rookie title under his belt, Baguio’s Formula 4 driver Iñigo Anton heads to Sepang as the only Filipino on the grid, taking on the Malaysian circuit with an F1 crowd watching

items: Iñigo Anton, a young Filipino racer, is set to compete in the Formula Trophy Malaysia at Sepang, coinciding with the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix, marking a significant opportunity in his career.

Having previously raced in Sepang and won the rookie championship in the 2025 Formula 4 Southeast Asia series, Anton is familiar with the challenging circuit and aims to perform well amidst increased visibility and competition.

With support from sponsors and guidance from experienced figures in motorsport, Anton's participation in this high-profile event represents not only a personal milestone but also a chance to showcase Filipino talent on an international stage.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

BAGUIO CITY, Philippines – Iñigo Anton has raced in Sepang before. He has stood on its podium, battled other young drivers around its fast corners, and ended his 2025 Formula 4 campaign as the Southeast Asian series’ rookie champion.
When he returns in October, however, the same track will feel very different.
Formula 1 will be there.

The Baguio racer is set to compete in the Formula Trophy Malaysia at the Petronas Sepang International Circuit from October 2 to 4, a Formula 4 event running as a support race during the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

“This is the biggest opportunity of my career so far,” Anton said during a recent media briefing in Baguio. “The competition will be fierce, but we’ve put in the preparation. I’m ready to leave everything on the track and do the Philippines proud.”

blocks.caption: Iñigo Anton prepares for a race during his 2025 Formula 4 Southeast Asia campaign. All photos courtesy of Karen Anton

blocks.text: The weekend itself is unusual. Formula 1 announced in July that Sepang would host the 2026 Bahrain Grand Prix after the original Bahrain race could not proceed earlier in the year amid the situation in the Middle East. The arrangement puts Formula 1 back at the Malaysian circuit for the first time since 2017.
For Anton, it creates a rare opening: a Formula 4 race on the same weekend, at the same circuit with the highest level of single-seater racing.

Sepang is hardly unfamiliar territory. Anton competed there extensively during the 2025 Formula 4 Southeast Asia Championship, finishing third in the overall drivers’ standings and winning the Rookie Cup for BlackArts Racing. The official championship results list him as the top rookie of the season.
That experience matters because Sepang is not an easy circuit to learn on the fly.

The 5.543-kilometer track combines long straights, heavy braking zones, and fast corners, with heat, humidity, and sudden rain adding another layer of unpredictability. Formula 1 itself describes Sepang as one of the championship’s most demanding circuits.
Anton will race car No. 33 under Axle Sports, according to his camp, which also said he is expected to be the only Filipino driver on the grid.

blocks.caption: Iñigo Anton celebrates on the podium with the Philippine flag during his 2025 Formula 4 Southeast Asia campaign. Anton finished the season third overall and the championship’s top rookie.

blocks.text: The Formula Trophy Malaysia opens in Sepang on the Formula 1 weekend before returning to the circuit for two more rounds in November and December. The difference this time is everything’s happening around the race.

An F1 weekend brings a far larger crowd, international teams, sponsors, media, and motorsport decision-makers into the same paddock. For young drivers trying to move up the single-seater ladder, visibility can matter almost as much as results.
That is why Anton’s family sees the October race as more than another start on his calendar.

“With Formula 1 making its much-anticipated return to Sepang, the global spotlight will be brighter than ever,” said his race manager and mother, Karen Anton. “Having our local racing pride fly the Philippine flag on this grand stage is a testament to years of grit.”
Anton’s rise has been unusually long for someone still in his early 20s.

He began racing as a child under the guidance of his father, veteran racer Carlos Anton, progressing from karting and local circuit racing to international competition. By 13, he was already attracting attention for competing against much older drivers.
The University of Baguio later recognized him after he was named the Automobile Association Philippines’ 2022 Driver of the Year for circuit racing.
He eventually moved into single-seaters and made his Formula 4 Southeast Asia debut in 2023. By 2025, he was competing in his first full F4 season, taking podiums and eventually the rookie crown.

The road has not been perfectly smooth. Anton has had disqualifications, difficult weekends, and races where pace did not translate into the result he wanted. That is part of what makes the Sepang opportunity significant.
He is no longer arriving simply as the young Baguio racer trying Formula 4. He returns with a full season behind him, experience at Sepang, and a clearer idea of what international racing demands.

blocks.caption: Iñigo Anton (center) with his mother and race manager Karen Anton, and father and coach Carlos Anton, during a media briefing in Baguio City on September 21, 2026.

blocks.text: His preparation for October includes physical conditioning, simulator work, and technical coaching. His camp said he has also been working under former Malaysian Formula 1 driver Alex Yoong, whose BlackArts Racing operation fielded Anton during his 2025 F4 campaign. The championship itself identified BlackArts as Yoong’s team.
Carlos Anton, who remains his son’s coach, said the job now is to translate preparation into race pace.
“He has the pace, he has the discipline, and he’s ready to race with the best,” he said.
Anton’s camp is openly targeting a strong result, even a podium, but the significance of the weekend is not limited to where he finishes.

Formula 4 is one of the entry points into the FIA’s single-seater development ladder. The cars are slower and less sophisticated than Formula 1 machines, but the discipline teaches the same fundamentals young drivers need as they move upward: qualifying pace, race craft, tire management, technical feedback, and consistency under pressure.
Very few Filipino drivers reach this stage, and fewer still get to race during a Formula 1 weekend.

Anton knows the opportunity may not come often. His sponsors include Motul, Alpinestars, Yokohama, Blu Coffee Distributors, Time Master Watches, Infiniteserv International Corporation, and Axle Sports, support that has helped sustain a career in one of sport’s most expensive disciplines.
The Philippine flag on his helmet and racing suit will therefore represent more than hometown pride when he reaches Sepang.
It will also mark how far a racer who learned his craft in Baguio has traveled.
Anton has already raced this circuit.
This time, the world of Formula 1 will be watching from just a few garages away. – Rappler.com

articles.title: OpenAI tools post user images from ChatGPT online
articles.summary: OpenAI said it found 53 cases in which user-uploaded image links on ChatGPT were shared with third-party websites. The company said it had removed most of these links.

image.caption: OpenAI said it had removed most of the leaked content and was working to remove the restImage: Jakub Porzycki/NurPhoto/IMAGO

blocks.text: Artificial intelligence giant OpenAI on Friday acknowledged that its AI tools had posted images users provided to ChatGPT on online sites, without the company's knowledge, in yet another example of AI agents operating outside of their confines.
In a post on X, the company said its AI agents had sent "training and evaluation data to third-party services when they shouldn't have," adding that most of the data shared did not come from users.
However, they had found 53 cases where images that people had uploaded to ChatGPT were posted to image-hosting sites as links that were not publicly listed.
"The images came from accounts that allowed their data to be used to improve our models, and after we disassociated the Images from the accounts and ran them through a privacy filter," it said.
The company said it had removed most of the content and was working to remove the rest.
Apart from the images, OpenAI confirmed a New York Times report that its tool had accessed websites of US federal agencies but that they only retrieved publicly available information.
Tech giant OpenAI heads for Wall Street
Rising fear of rogue AI

The latest disclosure comes amid heightened global concerns about AI systems escaping human control and hacking into external websites, as well as industry calls for a slowdown on AI development — a move which OpenAI said it supports.
Friday's post also clarified that the cases of unauthorized sharing occurred before a fresh round of safeguards were implemented over a month ago.

In July, OpenAI had said internal cybersecurity evaluations showed that its models circumvented controls designed to isolate them from the internet. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman on Friday said it was "still the most severe event we've seen."

"We are continuing to review agent activity in research and evaluation runs, working backward month by month starting from the Hugging Face incident," OpenAI said in a safety blog post on Friday, adding that it would "provide further updates" in time.
How US, China could end the AI race
Investigation finds OpenAI agents attempting hacks

AI evaluator and research lab Transluce on Friday said that it also found that AI agents, appearing to originate from OpenAI, attempted a rudimentary hack on the US Department of Education website for the department's civil rights office. The agents did not succeed, according to the independent investigation.

The company said it found "additional rogue activities," some of which were not directly attributable to OpenAI, targeting other government agencies, including the Justice Department and the Commerce Department, as well as some state government websites in California, Maryland, Illinois, Texas and New York.

articles.title: ‘Queenie’ almost a typhoon
articles.summary: Severe Tropical Storm Queenie (international name: Surigae) is now nearing typhoon strength as it moves over the Philippine Sea, state weather bureau PAGASA said.

blocks.text: September 26, 2026 | 1:49pm
Satellite rendering shows Severe Tropical Storm Queenie (international name: Surigae) taken as of 10:40 a.m. of Sept. 26, 2026.
PAGASA via Facebook
MANILA, Philippines — Severe Tropical Storm Queenie (international name: Surigae) is now nearing typhoon strength as it moves over the Philippine Sea, state weather bureau PAGASA said.
In its 11 a.m. bulletin on Saturday, September 26, the state weather bureau said Queenie was carrying maximum sustained winds of 110 kilometers per hour near the center, with gusts of up to 135 kph.
It is moving west-northwestward at 10 kph.
The center of Queenie was estimated at 575 kilometers east-northeast of Itbayat, Batanes.
PAGASA said strong to storm-force winds extend outward up to 280 kilometers from Queenie's center.
No tropical cyclone wind signal is currently in effect.
Queenie is unlikely to directly affect the country's land areas throughout the forecast period.
Sea conditions
PAGASA said moderate seas of up to 2 meters are expected over the seaboards of Isabela, the northern seaboard of Batanes and the eastern seaboard of Davao Oriental in the next 24 hours.
Mariners of motorbancas and similarly sized vessels were advised to take precautionary measures while venturing out to sea and, if possible, avoid navigation under these conditions.
Other coastal waters are expected to have wave heights of less than 2 meters.
Track, intensity
Queenie will continue decelerating while turning northward in the next 12 hours before turning north northeastward by Sunday morning, September 27.
On the forecast track, the center of Queenie is expected to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility between Sunday afternoon and evening.
Outside the PAR, Queenie will accelerate northeastward toward the sea south of mainland Japan.
PAGASA said Queenie will likely intensify into a typhoon on Saturday and strengthen further while moving over the sea south of the Okinawa Islands.
After reaching peak intensity, Queenie is expected to weaken by Monday, September 28.

articles.title: No ghost projects in Taguig, DPWH chief Vince Dizon tells Alan Cayetano
articles.summary: Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon said that based on his agency's ongoing investigation, it has yet to find a ghost or non-existent infrastructure project in Taguig…

blocks.text: Published September 26, 2026 1:47pm

Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) Secretary Vince Dizon said that based on his agency's ongoing investigation, it has yet to find a ghost or non-existent infrastructure project in Taguig City.
During the Senate hearing Friday on the DPWH budget for 2027, Senator Alan Peter Cayetano asked Dizon if the department has identified a ghost project in the former's political bailiwick of Taguig.
"Wala po. Sa aming imbestigasyon, wala po," Dizon replied. (There is none. Based on our investigation, there is none.)
According to DPWH Undersecretary Ricardo Bernabe III, the agency has so far listed 107 projects in Taguig, all of which have accomplishments.

"So I'll stop there. Mayroon na kayong... And everyone's open to look at it. The media, any investigating. Because I myself want to know kung may ghost. Kasi simula nu'ng nangyari itong flood control, tanong kami nang tanong sa sarili naming lugar. Kahit hindi ako taga-DPWH," Cayetano said.

(So I'll stop there. You have… And everyone's open to look at it. The media, any investigating. Because I myself want to know if there is a ghost. Ever since this flood control happened, we keep aksing if there are in our area, even if I am not from the DPWH.)
Cayetano has been embroiled in a verbal feud with Senator Ping Lacson after the two traded corruption allegations since July. Lacson has since then started a probe into Taguig projects.
Lacson said that his probe into Taguig City ghost projects opened a "cauldron of worms" upon meeting with officials from the Philippine Reclamation Authority (PRA). — VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Gracioso allegations vs VP Sara Duterte should be taken 'seriously' --Adiong
articles.summary: House prosecution panel spokesperson Rep. Zia Adiong of Lanao del Sur said Saturday that claims that Vice President Saa Duterte received suitcases containing billions of pesos “have to be taken…

blocks.text: Published September 26, 2026 1:43pm

House prosecution panel spokesperson Rep. Zia Adiong of Lanao del Sur said Saturday that claims that Vice President Saa Duterte received suitcases containing billions of pesos “have to be taken seriously.”

"These allegations should be taken seriously. Kasi nagpakita siya... I think anyone who comes out with that serious and grave allegations should be taken seriously, and I think the NBI is taking cognizance of this," Adiong said in Bea Pinlac's report.

On Friday, dismissed policeman Rodulfo Gracioso Jr. said that he delivered suitcases containing cash to Vice President Sara Duterte, former President Rodrigo Duterte, and Davao City 1st District Representative Paolo Duterte as ordered by former Speaker Lord Allan Velasco.
Gracioso supposedly served as a security officer for Velasco.
The new allegations, according to Adiong, could also be related to VP Duterte’s alleged unexplained wealth, which is among the articles of impeachment.

“It’s not entirely connected with the articles of impeachment… I do not think it would directly impact the ongoing impeachment trial, but what I can tell you is that this is something that erodes the reputation of those mentioned... Separate po ‘yung impeachment trial,” he added.
The NBI has said that it is investigating Gracioso's claims.
GMA News has sought comments through phone calls and messages from Pulong Duterte, Rodrigo Duterte, and Velasco since Thursday, but they have yet to give any.
Sara denies
Vice President Sara Duterte on Saturday has issued a statement saying she does not know Gracioso
"Mga kababayan, I do not know Rodulfo Gracioso Jr., nor have I ever received any money from him," Duterte said in a statement.
"My lawyers are awaiting an official copy of the Gracioso affidavit from the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) so they can begin working on the cases to be filed against him," she added.
"Once we are done dismantling the lies contained in his testimony, it will end up in the trash bin—just like the one from Ramil Madriaga," Duterte said.
The vice president said Gracioso's allegation is "another media stunt," adding that the Marcos administration is bent on bringing her down.

"This is nothing more than another media stunt, an attempt to breathe life into a faltering impeachment case. The desperation of the administration to bring me down, push for Charter Change, prevent the 2028 elections, and cling to power is becoming increasingly diabolical," she said.
"The people want Marcos to take a public drug test. The people want Marcos to answer for the flood control scandal. The people want change," Duterte said. —with reports from Bea Pinlac/ VAL, GMA News

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — On September 19, the White House denied access to journalists from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico, following through with US President Donald Trump‘s announcement that he would ban them from the building’s grounds.

All three news outlets separately said their teams’ press passes were confiscated when their journalists went to the White House. They have signaled that they may contest the ban on the grounds that it conflicts with the US Constitution’s First Amendment protections for free speech and a free press.

On September 21, US District Judge Tim Kelly orders the Trump administration to immediately return the outlets’ press passes and blocked officials from enforcing the ban for 14 days. On September 24, the White House said it has reinstated access to the three news organizations.

At the Senate, the impeachment court voted on September 23 to lower the voting threshold for the conviction of Vice President Sara Duterte. The ruling, which passed with 13 votes in favor and one against, approved the September 8 appeal of Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo seeking to overturn the July 6 ruling of Presiding Officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero.

Meanwhile, former overseas Filipino worker and human trafficking victim Mary Jane Veloso was released from the Correctional Institution for Women on September 25. This comes a day after President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. granted her absolute pardon, after more than a decade in detention.

articles.title: White House bars CNN from travelling with Trump on Air Force One
articles.summary: CNN was scheduled to fly with US President Donald Trump for his trip to Tennessee on Saturday.

blocks.text: US broadcaster CNN has been barred from travelling with President Donald Trump on Air Force One for a trip to Tennessee on Saturday.
The move is the latest in a battle between the White House and the media after it was forced to lift its ban on some news outlets.

CNN was scheduled to fly with Trump for his trip to Tennessee for a college American football game until a note released on Friday night by the White House did not list the broadcaster on the media schedule.
The BBC has requested comment from the White House.
CNN has reported that no other outlet was listed as replacing them in the president's tentative schedule.
Last week Trump banned CNN, Politico and MS NOW journalists from the White House after accusing them of writing "fiction or lies" about his administration.
All three media outlets said they were pursuing legal action, and accused Trump of violating their constitutional rights to free speech and freedom of the press.

Four television networks that have a daily rotation of White House coverage along with CNN - ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC - had paused their broadcasts of the president in solidarity with the banned outlets.
The White House then launched its own streaming channel, Trump TV, ahead of the United General Assembly in New York.
A federal judge has since ruled Trump barring news outlets from the White House was likely unconstitutional and the administration had to let them back in, at least for now.
However, the White House still denied entry to some CNN and MS NOW reporters assigned to cover arrivals for a state dinner for Chinese leader Xi Jinping on Thursday.

A White House communications account earlier posted on X that "contrary to what the Fake News wants you to believe, they don't just get to have free rein into every part of the White House, every event, and every press call".
Regular US television coverage resumed on Friday after White House officials allowed reporters entry.
The president is set to attend a football game between University of Tennessee vs University of Texas College at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville from midday on Saturday.
